title: Custom RequestValidationError & HTTP Status Code Mapping

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When a user submits bad data, FastAPI's default response can be long and technical. A custom exception handler is a polite translator: it catches the error and reformats it into clean, consistent JSON error messages matching your company's exact standard.
progressiveExplaining.junior: You register custom exception handlers in FastAPI using `@app.exception_handler(ExceptionClass)`. To customize default 422 validation errors, override `RequestValidationError`: `@app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError) async def validation_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError): return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={'errors': ...})`. You can also create custom business domain exceptions.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, FastAPI handles exceptions through Starlette's `ExceptionMiddleware`. Custom handlers allow decoupling internal domain exceptions (e.g. `ItemOutOfStockError`) from HTTP transport status codes (`409 Conflict`). By intercepting both `HTTPException` and `RequestValidationError`, you ensure all API errors across the application conform to an enterprise RFC 7807 (Problem Details) or custom standard envelope.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: `ExceptionMiddleware` wraps the ASGI call in a `try...except` block. When an error is raised, it looks up the exception's class hierarchy in `app.exception_handlers`. It invokes the matching async handler `async def handler(request, exc)` and returns the resulting `Response` object before Starlette sends HTTP headers.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `fastapi.HTTPException` and `starlette.exceptions.HTTPException`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of FastAPI vs Starlette exception inheritance.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `fastapi.HTTPException` inherits from `starlette.exceptions.HTTPException`. The difference is that `fastapi.HTTPException` accepts a `headers` parameter and allows passing any JSON-serializable structure to `detail` (dict, list, string), whereas Starlette's only accepts strings. Always import and raise `fastapi.HTTPException` in FastAPI applications.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If you register an exception handler specifically for `starlette.exceptions.HTTPException`, it will catch `fastapi.HTTPException` too, but accessing `exc.headers` may require `getattr`.

interviewGotchas.question: Why does an exception raised inside a background task NOT trigger an `@app.exception_handler`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of lifecycle execution boundaries in ASGI.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Because `BackgroundTasks` execute **after the HTTP response has already been sent and the connection is closed**. By the time the background task executes, the HTTP status code and response body are already committed to the client socket, so the exception handler cannot construct a new HTTP error response.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Always wrap code inside background tasks in custom `try...except` logging blocks.
